sentences.text: Kalthifrons possessed a short, roughly triangular skull that was flattened, resembling the shape of modern crocodiles.
The most distinctive trait of this animal is its frontal bone, which created a space between the eyes much wider than seen in Australosuchus.
Its skull table was flat and trapezoid with elliptical openings similar to those found in Trilophosuchus, while the back part of the skull table was narrow.
The lower jaw featured a flat underside offset by a sharp bend, and the eye sockets were positioned far forward on the head.
Large eye sockets with diameters greater than the distance between them sat alongside elongated, irregularly triangular lacrimal bones.
The preserved skull measures approximately 44.7 cm in length from the broken snout tip to the quadrate bone.
Fossils of Kalthifrons and turtles found at the Golden Fleece Locality are interpreted as a mass death assemblage caused by the drying up of a watering hole.
The genus name combines the Dieri word for 'spear' and the Latin word for 'forehead', while the species name reflects the Golden Fleece Locality.
The genus Kalthifrons was described by Yates and Pledge in 2017 as an extinct group containing only one species.
Remains were recovered from the Mampuwordu Sand Member of the Tirari Formation on the western shores of Lake Palankarinna in South Australia's Lake Eyre Basin.
The holotype, specimen SAM P35062, consists of a cranium and two mandibular rami, while the Golden Fleece Locality yielded isolated remains including teeth, osteoderms, and vertebrae.
The holotype preserves three teeth in the left premaxilla, though the missing bone suggests additional teeth were originally there, and teeth at the front of the maxilla were closely spaced.

Evidence of a large reception pit between the sixth and seventh maxillary teeth indicates that some degree of tooth interlocking existed, while the few known tooth crowns are short, blunt, and broadly rounded.
Better-preserved teeth from the same locality as the holotype are taller, more pointed, less compressed, and have a gentle inward curvature compared to the posterior teeth.

Kalthifrons was larger than many other mekosuchines like Trilophosuchus and Mekosuchus, and although smaller than large mekosuchines like Baru and Paludirex, it was larger in total body length than dwarf forms such as Volia, Trilophosuchus, and Mekosuchus.
Both Kalthifrons and Tirari Crocodylus are interpreted as generalist semi-aquatic predators with similar skull forms, supporting a competition hypothesis.

The preserved skull shows that better-preserved teeth from the same locality as the holotype are taller, more pointed, less compressed, and have a gentle inward curvature compared to the posterior teeth.
The genus Kalthifrons is monotypic, containing only the single species Kalthifrons aurivellensis, which is the type species of the genus and is classified within the subfamily Mekosuchinae.
Kalthifrons lived during the Pliocene epoch, specifically the Zanclean age, between 5.333 and 3.6 million years ago.
Researchers attribute the varying phylogenetic positions of Kalthifrons to poor fossil preservation and a limited number of usable anatomical characters.

It is debated whether competition with the invasive genus Crocodylus caused the extinction of Kalthifrons, as there is no direct evidence supporting this hypothesis, while an alternative hypothesis suggests Kalthifrons went extinct due to ongoing aridification during the late Neogene and Quaternary rather than competition with Crocodylus.
